A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OA-Adapter research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments, baseline comparisons, parameter-efficiency measurements and ablations using T5 models.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds SuperNI, LLaMA-7B, regularization-sensitivity, replay and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The core adapter architecture, trainable threshold and orthogonality objective remain unchanged in Equations 1–11. v2 adds an evaluated OA-Adapter+Replay training variant in Appendix A.7, while explicitly excluding replay from the final default approach.

E1.justification: v2 adds 15 SuperNI tasks spanning dialogue generation, information extraction, answer generation, summarization and sentiment analysis, substantially extending the classification-focused coverage. The original standard and 15-task benchmarks remain; the latter is renamed Long Sequence Benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 removes SeqFT, EWC, LwF, PerTaskFT and MTL comparisons and adds SAPT+Replay and SAPT+ARM comparisons in Appendix A.7. Inc-Adapter and O-Adapter aggregate scores reappear under component-ablation labels in Table 2, so their evidence is not wholly deleted.

E3.justification: v2 adds forward/backward transfer metrics, ROUGE-L evaluation for generative SuperNI tasks, two SuperNI task orders and LLaMA-7B testing. Additional protocols include an orthogonality-coefficient sweep and timing measurements with bottleneck dimension 24. Existing classification splits, training epochs and batch sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends component-ablation evidence to SuperNI and adds orthogonality-coefficient sensitivity, replay compatibility, GPU-memory/training-time comparisons and isolated orthogonality-overhead analysis. The original threshold experiments, forgetting curves and budget-allocation heatmaps are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results average three runs with different task orders. Neither adds seed identifiers, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests, and v2 does not document an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: OA-Adapter's original benchmark means remain 76.0 and 69.2. However, ProgPrompt's long-sequence mean changes from 77.9 to 63.2 without explanation, reversing its ranking against OA-Adapter. New results include SuperNI scores, transfer metrics, LLaMA-7B comparisons, sensitivity, replay and resource measurements. Many original per-order comparison entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 introduces mathematical definitions of forward and backward transfer in Section 4.1; v1 defined only final average accuracy. The adapter equations and gradient derivations remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 expands the existing column-space explanation without introducing a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed empirical advantage to two 15-task benchmarks, including SuperNI. The central claim of integrating adaptive budgets with orthogonal continual learning, and the reported 58.5% parameter saving, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of output-space orthogonality, generative-task difficulty, replay compatibility and its resource tradeoffs, and overhead scaling. It removes v1 Appendix A.6's explicit training-task-ID limitation and unresolved memory-recovery caveat, along with discussion of performance gaps to PerTaskFT and MTL.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses validation-based selection of the orthogonality coefficient, SuperNI task identifiers and orders, and runtime/memory measurements. Section 6 states that code was submitted as supplementary material and promises a later GitHub release; actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Most existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SuperNI, SAPT and evaluation metrics, while removing the EWC and LwF references. The detailed SoRA comparison is condensed, but the central positioning relative to orthogonal-subspace and adaptive-budget methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the paper: related work moves from Appendix A.1 into Section 2 and is rewritten, experimental discussions and appendices are reordered, and reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added. The title and numerous explanatory passages are also revised.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned from per-order accuracy comparisons into benchmark-wise AA/FWT/BWT columns. Ablation evidence is separated into Table 2, other tables are added or expanded, and parameter-budget columns are reformatted. All seven figures remain, but are relocated or resized; the main forgetting plot becomes a smaller text-wrapped display with revised legend presentation.

improvement.justification: SuperNI, LLaMA-7B, transfer metrics and sensitivity/cost analyses broaden v1's validation substantially. However, v2 removes useful comparison anchors and an explicit limitation, while the unexplained ProgPrompt score change reverses an important ranking. New reporting also has inconsistencies: only two SuperNI orders accompany the three-run/different-order statement, and Table 11's times average 0.016475 seconds rather than the reported 0.0179. These gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident judgment of net quality improvement.
